title: Worksheet 10: How the Internet Works
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: When you visit a website, your device is not simply "opening a file" — it is having a conversation with another computer somewhere else in the world. Your device, such as a laptop or phone, is called the "client." The client sends a request over the internet asking for a specific webpage. That request travels to a "server," which is a powerful computer that stores websites and is always ready to respond to requests. When the server receives the request, it sends the requested webpage's information back to the client, which then displays it on your screen as the website you see. This entire back-and-forth process usually takes less than a second, even though the server might be located thousands of miles away. This basic pattern, a client requesting information and a server responding, is called the "client-server model," and it is the foundation of how the internet works.
